title: Integrated Risk and Access Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This playbook consolidates core company-wide processes that intersect with risk and access: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel approvals, and internal templates. It is designed for product, engineering, security, finance, and people-ops stakeholders who operationalize these policies. The goal is to reduce friction, align decision rights, and ensure consistent controls while enabling fast delivery.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to company systems.
- Covers corporate (G Suite/Okta), cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP), production inference environments (Redwood runtime clusters), procurement up to $250k, and vendor contracts.
- Does not replace team-specific runbooks; it defines minimum required controls, approvals, and escalation paths.

Principles

1. Least privilege by default: grant the minimum access required and review privileges quarterly.
2. Separation of duties for procurement, approvals, and change execution for production systems.
3. Risk-based approach: higher-impact assets require stronger controls and additional approvals.
4. Transparent ownership: every service and dataset has an owner and documented SLA.

Roles and Responsibilities

- Service/Data Owners: maintain inventory, classification, retention, and access lists for their services/data.
- Requester: initiates access, change, procurement, or travel requests and provides business justification.
- Approvers: named approvers in Okta/Confluence workflows (team leads, security, finance depending on request type).
- Security Team: performs security reviews for vendor onboarding and high-risk changes.
- Finance/Procurement: validates vendor terms, issues POs, and enforces spending controls.
- People-Ops: reviews and approves travel and contractor engagements.

Access and Permissions

Principles and Categories

- Temporary Access (<= 30 days): used for short-term tasks; requires ticket in Access Jira (ACCESS-xxx) and approval from service owner and security for prod scopes.
- Role-based Access: roles defined in Okta groups and mapped to least-privilege IAM policies in cloud accounts.
- Permanent Access: requires manager and service owner sign-off with quarterly attestation.

Access Request Process (step-by-step)

1. Create an ACCESS ticket in Jira using template: purpose, duration, resources, and justification.
2. Notify direct manager and service owner via the Jira approvals workflow.
3. Security performs a risk review for production or data-classified-as-sensitive.
4. Upon approval, IAM or cloud owner grants access and records change with a link to the ticket.
5. Ticket is closed only after successful attestation entry confirming access removal for temporary grants.

Approval Matrix (summary)

| Resource Type | Typical Approver(s) | Additional Controls |
|---------------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Non-prod infra | Team Lead | Access logs retained 30 days |
| Prod infra | Service Owner + Security | Just-in-time access, 30-day max for temporary |
| Sensitive data (PII) | Data Owner + Security + Compliance | DLP review, encrypted-at-rest, restricted egress |
| Billing/Finance | Finance Manager | MFA enforced, audit trail |

Quarterly Access Reviews

- Owners run quarterly reviews using the Access Review template in Confluence and validate group membership in Okta.
- Findings flagged as high risk are escalated to Security and People-Ops for remediation within 14 days.

Change Management

Scope and When to Use

- All changes affecting production inference clusters, routing policies, model rollouts, or IAM policies must follow the change process. Non-production changes follow lightweight reviews documented per team.

Change Categories

1. Standard change: pre-authorized, routine, low-risk (e.g., config tweaks under established runbooks).
2. Normal change: requires planning, testing, and approval via Change Advisory Board (CAB).
3. Emergency change: applied to stop or remediate an outage; retrospective review required.

Normal Change Process

1. Submit a CHANGE ticket (CHANGE-xxx) with scope, rollback plan, test plan, and scheduled window.
2. Service owner and QA approver sign-off.
3. CAB review if change impacts SLOs or cross-team dependencies (CAB meeting twice weekly).
4. Implement in the scheduled window, perform post-deploy validation, and mark as completed in the ticket.

Emergency Change Process

1. For urgent mitigation, designated on-call may implement an emergency change after alerting stakeholders via #incidents and creating an incident-linked CHANGE ticket.
2. Emergency changes must be small, reversible, and documented with immediate post-change tests.
3. A post-implementation review (PIR) is required within 72 hours.

Change Window and SLOs

- Standard maintenance windows: Sat 02:00-06:00 UTC for non-critical infra optimizations.
- Target change success rate: >= 98% for normal changes (measured by rollback frequency and incident correlation).

Data Management

Data Classification

- Public: safe to share externally.
- Internal: company-internal operational data.
- Confidential: business-sensitive (pricing, roadmaps).
- Sensitive/Restricted: PII, regulated data, or customer data requiring contractual protection.

Minimum Controls by Class

| Classification | Encryption | Access Control | Retention |
|----------------|------------|----------------|----------|
| Public | Optional | Broad | 1 year or less |
| Internal | At rest recommended | Company employees | 3 years default |
| Confidential | Encrypt at rest | Role-based | 7 years or per contract |
| Sensitive/Restricted | Encrypt in transit & at rest, KMS | Approved list + DLP | Per contract/region |

Data Lifecycle and Retention

- Owners must maintain a Data Inventory entry in Confluence with classification, retention policy, and deletion procedure.
- Automated retention policies should be implemented where possible (e.g., S3 lifecycle rules).

Data Access Auditing

- All access to Sensitive/Restricted data is logged centrally (CloudTrail/Stackdriver + internal audit index).
- Security runs monthly anomaly detection on access patterns; findings go to owners with a 14-day remediation SLA.

Procurement and Expenses

Spending Thresholds and Approvals

- Operational purchases < $5k: requestor + manager approval.
- Purchases $5k - $50k: requestor + manager + finance procurement review.
- Purchases $50k - $250k: requestor + manager + finance procurement + legal review.
- > $250k: Executive sponsor, legal, security, and finance sign-off; board notification for strategic vendors.

Procurement Flow (high level)

1. Initiate a PR in Procurement portal with cost center, justification, vendor, and term.
2. Finance validates budget and issues a PO after vendor KYC/security review.
3. Legal approves contract templates for > $50k or any vendor storing Redwood data.
4. Vendor receives PO and onboarding packet; procurement tracks SLA for delivery and invoicing.

Expense Reimbursement

- Use the Expenses system with receipts attached within 30 days. Travel advances require pre-approval. Per diem is available for multi-day travel; see the Travel section for limits.

Vendor Management and Onboarding

Vendor Risk Tiers

- Low (e.g., office supplies): minimal review.
- Medium (SaaS without customer data): procurement + finance + vendor questionnaire.
- High (hosts customer data, production access or critical infra): security assessment, legal standard or negotiated contract, periodic SOC2/ISO evidence review.

Onboarding Checklist

1. Complete vendor intake form in the Procurement portal.
2. Security performs questionnaire and, if required, a penetration or architecture review.
3. Legal issues contract and data processing agreement (DPA) if applicable.
4. Finance issues PO and sets payment terms.

Vendor Monitoring

- High-risk vendors: quarterly evidence review and annual on-site or remote audit where contractually required.
- Contract renewals trigger a risk re-evaluation 90 days before expiry.

Travel Policy (summary)

Approvals and Booking

- Domestic travel: manager approval required.
- International travel: manager + People-Ops approval and export-control screening where applicable.
- Use approved travel vendors and book through the corporate travel portal; exceptions require written justification.

Per Diem and Reimbursement Caps

- Domestic per diem: $75/day.
- International per diem: country-by-country table maintained by People-Ops.
- Flights: coach/economy for trips < 6 hours; premium economy with manager approval for > 6 hours.

Safety and Compliance

- Employees traveling to high-risk regions must complete a mandatory travel safety briefing and register with People-Ops.

Internal Templates and Artifacts

Included in the Confluence space (links):
- Access request template (ACCESS-REQUEST.md)
- Change request template (CHANGE-REQUEST.md)
- Vendor intake form (VENDOR-INTAKE.md)
- Procurement PR template (PROC-REQUEST.md)
- Quarterly access review checklist (ACCESS-REVIEW.md)

Sample Access Request (brief)

Purpose: Temporary debugging access to inference cluster
Requester: jane.doe@redwood.com
Duration: 14 days
Resources: prod-cluster-01 (k8s namespace: inference-prod)
Justification: Investigate KV cache miss causing degraded latency for client X
Approvals: team lead + service owner + security

Escalation Paths

- Access issues: Service owner -> Security -> People-Ops escalation within 48 hours for stalled approvals.
- Procurement disputes: Procurement -> Finance Manager -> Head of Finance.
- Change-related incidents: Incident channel -> On-call -> Incident Commander -> Post-implementation review within 72 hours.

Measurement and Continuous Improvement

- Metrics to track: average access request time, percentage of emergency changes, time-to-procure (PO issuance), vendor risk score distribution.
- Quarterly review: People-Ops + Security + Finance meet to review metrics and update playbook.

Appendix A: Example Jira Fields

- ACCESS ticket fields: requester, target resource, duration, business justification, approvers, security flag.
- CHANGE ticket fields: owner, risk level, rollback plan, test checklist, scheduled window, CAB decision.

Appendix B: Quick Reference Contacts

- Security: security-oncall@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- People-Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- Legal: legal@redwood.com
